name: IEC address dependency (A)
summary: Dependency label A used on memory symbols to show which word of an array the address inputs select.
description: A dependency is used mainly on memory symbols. Address inputs are grouped, often with the binary grouping symbol, to produce internal affecting inputs A0 to An. Data inputs and outputs labelled A then act only on the selected word, so one symbol can represent an entire array.

Reading a memory symbol, start with the address grouping to see the range, then follow the A-labelled data terminals. TI's public overview shows an array of latches forming a small random-access memory using this method.
The notation does not give access time or organisation details beyond word count and width. Those are in the device data.
readingNotes: Find the address grouping and its range first.
Terminals labelled A act on the selected word only.
drawingChecklist: Show the address bus with its binary grouping.
Label affected data terminals with A.
State word count and width in the outline title.
distinction: M dependency selects modes, while A selects which of several identical words is accessed.
